summary: This resolution sets House debate rules and waives points of order for three measures: H.R. 6945 on state use of Social Security funds for pregnancy centers, H.R. 6359 requiring colleges to inform pregnant students of rights and resources, and H.J. Res. 140 disapproving a BLM land withdrawal rule in Minnesota.

scores.thoughts: H.R. 6945 clarifies state authority to direct existing TANF (title IV-A) funds to pregnancy centers. This affects how federal block-grant dollars may be spent but does not appropriate new funds or change overall spending levels, producing only a tangential link to government spending.
None of the three underlying measures alters tax rates, credits, or revenue provisions.
The measures touch pregnancy-related services and information but do not restructure insurance markets, Medicaid, or Medicare; any healthcare connection is incidental.
No provisions address firearms, background checks, or gun regulations.
No provisions relate to visas, border enforcement, or immigration status.

H.R. 6945 explicitly authorizes TANF funds for pregnancy centers, which are organizations whose mission is to steer women away from abortion. H.R. 6359 requires colleges to publicize resources for pregnant students, reinforcing a policy environment supportive of carrying pregnancies to term. These provisions therefore tilt toward restricting access to abortion.
No defense or military spending provisions appear.

H.J. Res. 140 disapproves a BLM land-withdrawal order protecting federal lands in Minnesota. Overturning the withdrawal opens the lands to mining and other development, directly limiting environmental protections.
H.R. 6945 expands permissible uses of TANF block-grant dollars (a core welfare program) to include pregnancy centers, thereby broadening rather than scaling back the social safety net.

H.R. 6359 imposes a new federal disclosure requirement on institutions of higher education regarding pregnant students. This constitutes additional federal involvement in postsecondary education, producing a modest negative score on the education scale.
No drug-enforcement or decriminalization provisions are present.
No sentencing, policing, or criminal-justice reforms are addressed.
No trade, tariff, or globalization measures appear.
The resolution and underlying bills do not alter deficits, debt ceilings, or fiscal targets.
No provisions address LGBTQ legal protections or exemptions.
No foreign-aid authorizations or reductions are involved.
No election-administration or voting-access provisions exist.
No technology, data-privacy, or platform-regulation content appears.
No labor, union, or workplace-flexibility provisions are present.

Pregnancy centers frequently operate from religious motivations, and authorizing TANF funds for them could indirectly benefit religious providers, but the bill text does not create or modify religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
